tasks.short: Estimate food consumption, obtain supplies and retrieve food from storage

steps.what: Read actual bookings, service plans and available stock information
Count usable ingredients and capture actual quantities and condition
Group existing sales quantities for the cook's selected comparable services
Estimate expected portions using bookings, comparability, season and the actual menu
Calculate ingredient requirements from chosen portions, recipe yields and captured usable stock
Select actual supply quantities and suitable products, resolving calculation exceptions
Prepare the actual supply request with quantities, units and delivery details
Check final quantities, food suitability, costs, delivery time and exact supplier destination
Send the exact checked supply order to the authorised supplier
Retrieve the selected usable food from storage using safe rotation and handling

tasks.design: Configure comparable-service totals in {OPS_SYSTEM} and a deterministic ingredient calculator using the cook's actual portion forecast and stock counts. Reuse requester defaults in {PROCUREMENT}, then keep the final food and order checks, supplier release and physical food retrieval with the cook.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual grouping and ingredient arithmetic sit between actual stock checks and uncertain demand decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing service records and verified recipe quantities can feed native totals and plain arithmetic without predicting demand with a model.
tasks.still_hard: Novel events, usable stock condition, recipe yields and uncertain walk-in demand.
tasks.human_edge: The cook adjusts portions for real service conditions and rejects unsuitable food or substitutions.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and repeated request headers; the cook still chooses portions and products within existing purchasing authority.

reach.task: Explain an ingredient shortfall for an upcoming service
reach.learn: Yield units, stock rotation and demand comparability

evidence.claim: Selected comparable-service totals and recipe-to-portion arithmetic can be deterministic while demand judgement and food condition remain human. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is the cook in a service cycle with actual supply ordering and food retrieval. The scenario includes manual sales grouping and ingredient arithmetic today; already automated totals earn no benefit. Shares are provisional E1 estimates, independent of the means prior.

The booking and till owners already produce service identifier, date, covers and dish quantities. In s1 the cook selects which prior services are comparable; s3 only groups that selection. The cook counts and captures ingredient identifier, quantity, unit and usable condition in s2. There is no free stock feed or automatic freshness judgement.

The recipe owner supplies ingredient quantities, units and verified yield; s5 multiplies by chosen portions and subtracts captured usable stock with explicit compatible units. Missing recipes, incompatible units or unrepresentative history stop the relevant calculation and retain manual repair in s4, s6 and s8. No invented ingredient substitution or allergen claim is generated.

Request defaults remove 1.98 of nine hours for repeated requester, cost centre and delivery address; 7.02 hours retain actual lines and correction. The real supplier send is one fully retained hour and separately gated after final content and supplier are checked in s8. Edits invalidate release. Any ordinary draft save is unchanged within entry time.

This cook already has delegated purchasing authority for the shown order. Otherwise add the real other-role approval rather than treating it as free. Native reports and forms are tested before code; retrieval time and food waste are not converted into labour savings.
unknowns: Are sales grouping and ingredient quantities still calculated manually?
Are recipe yields and stock units verified?
Does the cook have the stated purchasing authority?
research_questions: Do recipe and stock units support exact arithmetic without hiding stock-count capture?

already_counted.description: Demand judgement, calculation fallback and final food/order checks

incremental.description: Maintain recipe/unit mappings, comparable-service grouping and request defaults

approvals.approved_version: Exact final ingredients, quantities, units, prices, delivery details and supplier destination checked in s8; edits void release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten grouping hours, ten ingredient-calculation hours and 1.98 repeated-header hours, less two upkeep: 19.98 net, rounded down. Cautious case: a unique event has no comparable past services and needs all ten grouping hours and all nine request hours manually; the verified portion-to-ingredient arithmetic still removes ten, less two upkeep leaves eight.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult supervisory staff to plan menus around costs and special event needs

steps.what: Read and capture the actual event requirements and service constraints
Review the available recipes, existing costs and practical kitchen capacity
Consult supervisory staff about menu choices, costs and event-specific requirements
Agree the practical menu direction and identify unresolved requirements
Write the agreed menu and unresolved points in the actual planning document
Save the ordinary internal menu planning document

tasks.design: Reuse the actual event date, service and headcount from the existing brief in the internal {DOCS} menu-planning form. Retain the cook's consultation, practical choices and substantive plan writing; ordinary saving of that working document has no gate or saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The actual menu plan repeats event identifiers alongside individually agreed dishes and constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: A native document form can reuse the existing brief fields without generating culinary decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling event expectations, cost and what the kitchen can reliably serve.
tasks.human_edge: The cook anticipates practical service difficulties and discusses trade-offs with supervisors.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeated event headers, with menu choices and supervisory authority unchanged.

reach.task: Explain a menu's operational constraints to supervisory staff
reach.learn: Service capacity, recipe costs and event planning

evidence.claim: A native menu-planning form can reuse event headers while keeping consultation and actual dish selection human. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The cook's participation is the focal time; supervisory participation is not counted as cook savings. This case has an actual written internal menu plan used by the kitchen, not invented meeting minutes. Recipe costing is an existing input here, not a new calculation claimed inside the consultation.

The event organiser supplies event identifier, date, service, headcount and requirements in the real brief. The cook reads and captures clarifications in s1, reviews actual recipes and costs in s2 and agrees choices in s3-s4. No clean conversation transcript, inferred dietary restriction or new research service is assumed.

Reusing event, date and headcount removes 1.96 of fourteen plan-entry hours; 12.04 retain all dish choices, special requirements, unresolved issues, meaning checks and missing-header correction. Ordinary save is one fully retained ungated hour. Native document reuse is tested before code.

This is an internal planning document, not a published customer menu, allergen declaration or purchasing order. No release of those artefacts is named or credited. Shares and the header-entry estimate are E1 assumptions to measure.
unknowns: Is a written internal menu plan actually kept?
Which event requirements need further clarification?
research_questions: Does native brief-field reuse reduce actual entry without changing the agreed menu or omitting unresolved constraints?

already_counted.description: Substantive menu-plan entry, checking and missing-field correction

incremental.description: Check event-field reuse after planning-form changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 1.96 repeated-header hours less 0.4 upkeep: 1.56 net, rounded down. Cautious case: the event brief has no reusable identifiers or the menu form already fills them; retain all current writing and do not add a new mapping. Consultation and practical menu choices remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan menu items and determine their prices

steps.what: Choose actual menu items and portion sizes for the intended service
Capture and verify actual recipe quantities, yields and portion units
Select and verify the current supplier price list and applicable pack units
Copy matching supplier prices and pack units into the actual recipe costing sheet
Calculate recipe and portion costs using verified price, quantity and yield units
Calculate indicative menu prices from the approved cost target and applicable tax rule
Check costing meaning and exceptions, then choose commercially suitable final menu prices
Save the ordinary internal menu costing and chosen price record

tasks.design: Test native recipe costing in {OPS_SYSTEM}; otherwise map verified supplier prices from {PROCUREMENT} and apply explicit quantity, yield and target-price arithmetic. Keep recipe capture, source selection, exception repair and commercial price choice human, with the ordinary internal save unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier prices arrive separately from recipe quantities, with manual copying and arithmetic before a commercial price decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Exact item mapping and explicit costing formulas can calculate proposals without a model choosing the menu or declaring allergens.
tasks.still_hard: Real yields, supplier unit changes and customers' willingness to pay.
tasks.human_edge: The cook decides whether an arithmetic target fits the dish, service and customer expectations.

ambition.what: Reconsider the price of a specific dish when its verified main-ingredient price changes.

tasks.altitude: Less copying and costing arithmetic; commercial pricing authority remains as delegated today.

reach.task: Explain a dish's cost sensitivity to an ingredient change
reach.learn: Yield costing, unit conversions and contribution margins

evidence.claim: Apicbase links recipe costing to supplier price changes; this supports the costing capability, not the estimated local time saving.

assumptions: This focal cook actually plans dishes and prices them through a mixed manual costing workflow: supplier price copying into a sheet, followed by manual batch/portion and target-price arithmetic. The numbers are E1 scenario estimates, not measured baselines. Any formulas or integrations already running earn no new labour benefit.

The cook captures ingredient identifier, amount, unit, actual recipe yield and portion size in s2. The supplier supplies current item identifier, pack unit, price and effective date; the cook verifies the applicable source in s3. Finance or management already supplies the approved cost target and applicable tax rule. No inferred price, yield or tax interpretation is supplied free.

s4 requires exact identifiers and compatible explicit units. s5 applies verified recipe quantity times unit cost divided by verified portions; s6 applies the explicit approved cost target and tax rule. Missing yield, changed pack units, unmatched items and unsupported rules stop calculations; s7 retains manual recosting, source comparison, meaning checks and the actual price choice.

s8 is the ordinary internal author save at one fully retained percent with no approval gate. This task produces the actual internal costing and chosen prices; no customer menu publication, till-price release or allergen declaration is issued here. If those releases are part of local practice they must have their own priced final-version checks and actions.
Native recipe costing is tested before custom code. New customer-facing prices are not automatically activated and no food-waste reduction is counted as time saving.
unknowns: Which costing arithmetic and price copying is still manual?
Are recipe yields and supplier pack conversions reliable?
Who has authority to choose final menu prices and who releases them to customers?
research_questions: Can exact ingredient mapping and explicit units reproduce checked portion costs across a real supplier price-list change?

already_counted.description: Full source and costing exception checks, manual repairs and commercial price choice

incremental.description: Maintain supplier item/unit mappings and explicit costing rules

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes fifteen price-copy hours, fifteen portion-cost arithmetic hours and ten target-price arithmetic hours, less three upkeep: 37 net. Cautious case: a supplier's unstructured price sheet cannot be mapped, so all fifteen copying hours remain; verified quantities and manually entered prices still support the 25 calculation hours, less three upkeep leaves 22. Actual recipe capture and commercial choice remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce actual grouping, recipe arithmetic and repeated fields while keeping culinary choices, food checks and final supplier releases accountable.
reach: Explain ingredient shortfalls and dish cost sensitivity to a head cook
role.ambitious_version: A cook with more time for actual food and service decisions and less repeated calculation.
